complexity.correctness_reason: nums = [1] * 1000 (permitted by the constraints) forces recursion ~1000 levels deep and raises RecursionError under CPython's default limit.
complexity.notes: Short-circuits via max() over a generator, which is a neat idiom for any(). The recursion depth equals the path length, so deep inputs overflow CPython's default recursion limit. A far better O(n) time, O(1) space single pass exists via ||tracking the farthest index reachable so far||, or equivalently scanning from the end for ||the leftmost position that can reach the end||.
complexity.summary: Exhaustive recursion: from index 0, try every allowed first jump and recursively check the remaining suffix, returning True if any branch succeeds. Each call also slices the list, so up to O(2^n) calls each pay O(n) for the slice.
